Located in the heart of the Upper West Side of New York City, our flexible all-day tickets let you explore at your own pace. Designed for young learners ages 0–6 , CMOM’s ever-changing programs and exhibits make learning through play exciting. Whether it’s your first visit or your fiftieth, there’s always something new to discover. Get Tickets What’s On Today Admissions Admission to CMOM includes access to all exhibits and daily public programs. Stay and play as long as you like! Visitors can even leave and come back later in the same day—just ask for a return sticker from Security or Guest Services at the door! Tickets can be purchased online in advance or right before your visit, and you’ll save $1 when you book online. Walk-up tickets are also available but reserving ahead ensures your spot. Members enjoy unlimited visits and may use their membership cards for admission anytime . Learn more about discounted admission options here. Adults Tickets In-Person: $18 $17 Online Pricing Buy Tickets Children (Ages 1–18) Tickets In-Person: $18 $17 Online Pricing Buy Tickets Infant (Under 12 months old) Free Buy Tickets Senior (65 and over with ID) Tickets In-Person: $15 $14 Online Pricing Buy Tickets Visitor With Disabilities Tickets In-Person: $15 $14 Online Pricing Buy Tickets Members Free Included in Membership Learn More Know Before You Go We’re dedicated to joyful learning, creativity, and community—a place where children and families come together to explore, create, and play. To help ensure everyone has a safe, fun, and welcoming experience , please review our visitor guidelines and helpful FAQs . You’ll find important information on tickets, hours, museum policies, accessibility, and more—all organized in easy-to-browse sections to help you plan your visit. For general questions, please email us at [email protected] . If you know the department you need, you can find contact information—including email addresses and phone numbers—in the FAQ . What Age Group is CMOM Designed For? CMOM is designed especially for children ages 0–6, a time of important brain development and growth. Our hands-on exhibits and programs support early learning through play, creativity, and exploration. While older children may enjoy select exhibits and programs, most of our spaces are specifically created for toddlers, preschoolers, and early elementary-age kids. We encourage grown-ups to play too! Food & Drink To keep our exhibits clean, safe for play, and free of allergens, food and beverages are not allowed inside the building. We do allow baby formula and water, and there are water bottle refill stations by the restrooms. While CMOM does not offer a cafeteria, you are welcome to leave and return throughout the day to enjoy nearby dining options and discount offers. Strollers For your convenience, complimentary stroller and coat check is available at CMOM. To ensure a safe and comfortable experience for all visitors, strollers are not permitted in exhibit areas. School Field Trips Visiting with a group of 15 or more students, campers, or a large group? On weekdays we offer specially curated 90-minute guided tours led by our expert educators. Advanced reservations are required to ensure the best experience for your group. Visit our Guided Field Trips page and contact our team for more information. Accessibility CMOM is committed to being a welcoming space for all visitors. The Museum is wheelchair accessible. Please note that the lower level of the Dynamic H2O exhibition has limited accessibility. Personal care attendants accompanying visitors with disabilities receive free admission. We offer a fully accessible restroom on the Third Floor and an ambulatory accessible restroom on the Lower Level. We also have accessible elevators and stroller parking. If you need assistance during your visit, our staff is happy to help. Personal care attendants accompanying visitors with disabilities receive free admission. Sensory Kits are also available to borrow at no additional cost during your visit. Each kit is designed to help children regulate, refocus, and feel at ease, and includes: Over-the-ear headphones for noise reduction A sand timer to support transitions Fidget toys to encourage self-regulation and focus Kits are available at the Admissions desk and in PlayWorks on the 3rd floor. Simply check one out at the start of your visit and return it before you leave. Learn more about our Accessibility Programing. Museum Policies To ensure a safe and enjoyable visit for everyone, we’ve put together a set of visitor guidelines. You can learn more on this page . Questions? Please visit our Frequently Asked Questions page. You can also call us at 212-721-1223 or send us an email to [email protected] . The CMOM Experience Daily Programming From ever-changing themed activities to PlayWorks , our dedicated space for our youngest visitors, every experience is designed to engage children at the right developmental stage. With a rotating schedule of interactive programs, there’s always a reason to visit and discover something exciting! PlayWorks Schedule: Daily programs for our youngest learners 0–4, with activities changing regularly on weekdays and weekends. 10:30 am – 11:00 am: Circle Time 11:15 am – 12:15 pm: Mural Wall or Messy with Art 1:45 pm – 2:30 pm: Special Daily Program or Mural Wall 2:45 pm – 3:45 pm: Messy with Art 4:00 pm: Alphie’s Goodbye Storytime Events Calendar Explore Our Exhibits Explore four floors of hands-on, research based, interactive exhibits designed to spark curiosity, creativity, and a love of learning. View Our Exhibits Early Childhood Classes Designed to meet the needs of young learners, our classes offer your child an opportunity to immerse themselves in learning. Explore Early Childhood Classes Join the CMOM Community Become a member, support our mission, and stay connected with special events and exclusive perks. To help ensure everyone has a safe, fun, and welcoming experience , please review our visitor guidelines and helpful FAQs below . You’ll find important information on tickets, hours, museum policies, accessibility, and more — all organized in easy-to-browse sections to help you plan your visit. For general questions, please email us at [email protected] . If you know the department you need, you can find contact information—including email addresses and phone numbers—in the FAQ section below. Safe Space Policy & How to Reach Us Our shared commitment to kindness and respect CMOM is dedicated to providing a safe, welcoming, and respectful environment for all children and caregivers. Our mission is to foster curiosity, early development, and joy through inclusive, hands-on learning. We value the diversity of our community and expect all visitors to treat one another—and our staff—with respect and kindness, regardless of race, ethnicity, religion, national origin, gender identity, sexual orientation, or ability. To support a positive environment, we ask that visitors: Avoid verbal or physical confrontations Follow museum rules, including using designated stroller parking and no food/drink in exhibits Refrain from behavior that is threatening, disrespectful, discriminatory, or disruptive CMOM does not permit harassment, hate speech, racism, or any conduct that puts others at risk. Visitors who compromise the safety or well-being of others may be asked to leave, and in serious or repeated cases, access may be permanently revoked. Thank you for helping us ensure CMOM remains a safe and joyful space for all. Department Directory General Info: 212-721-1223 | [email protected] Ticketing | [email protected] Membership: 212-721-1234 | [email protected] Early Childhood Classes: 212-721-1226 | [email protected] Guided Group Visits: 212-721-1225 | [email protected] Development Department: 347-341-7458 | [email protected] Planning Your Visit When is the Museum open? October – June: Tuesday – Sunday, 10 am – 5 pm and federal holiday Mondays July – September: Monday – Sunday, 10 am – 5 pm Do I need a ticket to visit? Yes! Tickets to CMOM are easy to purchase and we participate with many programs to provide discounted and free admission . All visitors must have a ticket for entry. Visitors are allowed to re-enter the museum throughout the day of their visit. Members are required to show their membership card upon entry. Information on admission rates can be found in our Visit section. You can save one dollar by purchasing online in advance! Get Tickets! How do I visit with Cool Culture Pass? /If you have a Cool Culture Pass, please do the following for a seamless visit: The Cool Culture pass provides free general admission for up to 5 guests, including the card holder A valid photo ID is required to verify the Family Pass holder’s last name For groups of more than 5, admission fees apply to additional guests Nannies and caregivers may only use the Family Pass when the cardholder is present. Does CMOM have a cafe or dining facility on-site? No, CMOM does not have a café or dining area. However, you are welcome to leave and return throughout the day to enjoy nearby dining options where we have discounts available . Just ask for a return sticker from Security or Guest Services at the door! Can I bring food and drinks during my visit? No. For the safety and comfort of all visitors—especially those with food allergies— outside food and snacks are not permitted inside CMOM. We do allow water and baby formula . We kindly ask that you use spill-proof containers whenever possible to help protect our exhibits. We appreciate your cooperation in keeping our exhibits clean and safe for all children. Where can I store my stroller during my visit? We provide complimentary Stroller & Coat Check using Chexology, a digital system. This provides a more streamlined process for our visitors and attendants and everything is connected to your personal phone number! Is CMOM accessible for visitors with disabilities? Yes! CMOM is committed to providing an inclusive experience for all visitors. The museum is wheelchair accessible, however please note that the Lower Level of the Dynamic H2O exhibition has limited accessibility. We offer a fully accessible restroom on the Third Floor and an ambulatory accessible restroom on the Lower Level. We also have accessible elevators and stroller parking. If you need assistance during your visit, our staff is happy to help. Personal care attendants accompanying visitors with disabilities receive free admission. See more information about Accessibility on our website. Where are the restrooms located? Restrooms are available on the Lower Level and the Third Floor, both with infant changing tables. A fully wheelchair accessible restroom is available on the Third Floor, with an ambulatory accessible restroom on the Lower Level. How do I use my Access Pass and get a discounted ticket like Cool Culture? We are happy to work with a variety of programs like Cool Culture, etc. Just show your card at the desk and get your tickets. Currently you are not able to book these tickets on our website , but we always have tickets set-aside on-site for these partners! Check out our full list of partners. How do I redeem my ACM Reciprocal Ticket? All partner, discounted and complimentary tickets must be redeemed in person at our Admissions desk. For information on what programs we participate in and what offers each one provides, check out our page with more information. I left / lost something at the Museum! We have all been there! If we find items that are missing their owner, we keep lost items for 30 days at our Stroller & Coat Check area. To report or claim a lost item, please fill out our Lost & Found form . A team member will contact you if your item is found. Visitor Guidelines Can I help guide another child’s behavior if I see them doing something unsafe? We ask that adults only supervise their own children. If you have a concern about another visitor’s behavior, please notify a CMOM staff member—we’re here to help! First Aid kids are available on-site should they be needed. My child has special needs. Are there areas of the Museum suited for them? We know some children may need quieter areas. While CMOM can be lively, we encourage you to explore different spaces within the Museum or ask a staff member for suggestions on less busy areas. Sensory Kits are also available to borrow at no additional cost during your visit. Each kit is designed to help children regulate, refocus, and feel at ease. How can I make sure my child plays safely at CMOM? CMOM is designed for hands-on exploration, and we love seeing kids engaged and excited! To ensure a safe visit: Keep an eye on your child at all times. Encourage gentle play—exhibits and materials should be used with care. Climbing is only allowed in designated areas built for active play. Can my child run inside the Museum? We encourage movement and active play, but for safety, we ask that children walk while inside the Museum. There are plenty of fun spaces for climbing and jumping in designated areas! Why aren’t strollers allowed in exhibit areas? To ensure clear pathways and safe spaces for all visitors to move and play, we provide complimentary stroller check at the entrance. This helps keep our exhibits open and accessible for everyone. We also want to be sure that we have emergency exists always clear and not cause any fire and safety concerns. Health & Safety What happens if someone gets sick and we can't visit on the day of our tickets? We understand that illness happens, especially with our audience being little ones. Please reach out to [email protected] , and we will do our best to accommodate you to another date! For General Visitation tickets only. Registered programs and special events not included. Does my child need to wear shoes in all areas of the Museum? For health, safety, and cleanliness, we ask that children keep their shoes on throughout the museum, except in designated baby and toddler barefoot areas : Baby Grand Central (Lower Level) : Shoes must be removed before entering. Baby Steps in PlayWorks (Third Floor) : Babies and toddlers may be barefoot in this space. Does CMOM properly sanitize the spaces and provide hand sanitizer for guests? Yes! We take cleanliness very seriously and ensure that our spaces and the facility are cleaned regularly. We also provide hand sanitizer in a variety of easy-to-access locations for those who would like to use it. How often does CMOM clean the exhibits? We take cleanliness and hygiene seriously at CMOM! Our exhibits are cleaned daily throughout the day to ensure a safe and enjoyable experience for all visitors. Our Clean Team is on staff, regularly checking and sanitizing exhibit spaces, restrooms, and floors . You’ll often see them making their rounds to keep everything fresh and tidy, so you can focus on having fun! If you ever need assistance or notice something that needs attention, just let a staff member know—we’re happy to help What happens if my child gets hurt? In the case of anyone getting hurt, we have First Aid kits available on-site . Caregivers should ask any CMOM staff member for assistance and we are happy to provide help immediately. Membership & Discounts Do I need to reserve tickets in advance if I am a CMOM member? We encourage all members to reserve tickets online prior to arriving here at CMOM. Reserve your tickets here . Can I apply my admission ticket toward the cost of my CMOM Membership? Yes. This can be done within two weeks of your visit. Please visit our admission desk with your receipt or contact us at [email protected] or at 212-721-1234. Can I upgrade my Mini Membership? Yes. Up to one month after expiration, please contact us at [email protected] or at 212-721-1234. Can I purchase a membership as a gift? Yes. You can purchase a gift membership online here or contact us at [email protected] or 212-721-1234. What are the membership levels and benefits? Please visit the Membership page for more information. How do I find my digital membership card? You can access your digital membership card via the eMembership Card app using your Member ID for log in. Instructions to download your card can be found here. Can my caregiver bring the children to CMOM with my membership? Yes. Your caregiver can bring the children under your membership. Please provide the caregiver with a print or digital copy of the reservation confirmation email and the digital membership card. How can I update the information on my membership? Please contact us at [email protected] or 212-721-1234. What if I cannot find my membership ID? Please contact us at [email protected] or 212-721-1234, and we can retrieve your membership number. Can we transfer or get a refund on our membership? No. All memberships to the CMOM are nontransferable and nonrefundable. We are appreciative of your support as members, and your membership helps fund our mission and keeps CMOM accessible to all families. I am using my local library’s CMOM membership. What do I need to do? We encourage you to reserve a ticket on our website using the member ID provided by your library. Upon arrival, please present a copy of your reservation confirmation email and the pass provided to you by your library. I am a member of another Museum in the Association for Children’s Museums. Can I get discounted admission? Yes. Please email [email protected] for more information. My company is a corporate member. How can I reserve tickets? We encourage you to reserve a ticket on our website using the member ID provided by your company. Upon arrival, please present a copy of your reservation confirmation email. If you do not have a reservation, you must present a photo ID company badge upon arrival. Your caregiver can bring the children to the Museum under your company’s corporate membership. Please provide the caregiver with a print or digital copy of the reservation confirmation email. Does CMOM accept corporate matching gifts? Yes. You can double the amount of your membership contribution through your employer’s matching gifts program. For more information, please contact us at [email protected] or call us at 212-721-1234. Education & Classes Does CMOM provide classes? Yes! We have year round registered classes for children with our wonderful educators. You can sign-up for email to stay notified when registration opens, and visit our Education page to learn more. Are there drop-off camps? Currently, we do not provide drop-off camps. I would love to bring my school to CMOM! We have programs throughout the year for School Groups and Camps during the Summer. Sign-up for email and bookmark this page to learn more about the offerings. Would CMOM come to my school for a program? CMOM hosts a variety of School Residencies where we come to your schools and bring selected curriculum into your facility, for your students! Learn more about options here. Other Common Questions Can I host my child's birthday party at CMOM? At this time, we no longer offer birthday party services. However, we invite you to explore our variety of other programs and events designed for families and children. What else can we do around CMOM? The Upper West Side is filled with wonderful restaurants, parks, and other cultural institutions to visit. Plan your day at CMOM and include a visit to one of two great parks nearby. Riverside Park’s entrance on 83rd Street has a beautiful playground and ample benches for picnics. Three blocks east of the Museum is Central Park where there are ball fields, fountains, playgrounds and plenty of space for picnicking. CMOM has a list of restaurants with discounts and offers. Check them out for your next visit! Does CMOM donate memberships or free passes to my organization? CMOM recognizes that there are many wonderful organizations supporting children in the tri-state area. We are happy to donate a limited number of complimentary memberships. Please email [email protected] for more information. Is CMOM moving? Yes! CMOM will be moving in 2028 to a fabulous larger building on 96th and Central Park West. Until then we look forward to seeing you and your family at 83rd street! Learn more about our future home. You further agree that you and all Releasors release, waive, discharge, and covenant not to sue the Children’s Museum of Manhattan (CMOM) or any Releasees from any and all liability for any loss or damage, and any claim or demands, and any and all injuries incurred while visiting CMOM or any CMOM offsite location or participating in any CMOM activity, whether or not caused by the negligence of any of the Releasees during this and future visits to CMOM and any of its offsite locations, events and programs. You further agree to indemnify and hold harmless CMOM and the Releasees from and against any and all claims, causes of action or lawsuits, attorneys fees and expenses, for liability, damages, compensation or otherwise brought by you, and any child and anyone under your care or under your supervision or any other Releasor, including any attorneys; fees and related costs and medical bills and costs which may arise related to a visit to CMOM or any CMOM offsite location or event or participation in any CMOM activity on or off premises. Photography & Video Notice By purchasing a ticket and entering CMOM, you acknowledge and agree that you and any minors in your party may be photographed or recorded for promotional purposes. These images or videos may be used by CMOM in marketing materials, on our website, social media, advertising, and other non-commercial promotional content. CMOM will not sell or license any images of visitors for third-party commercial use. If you have concerns or wish to avoid photography, please speak to a staff member upon arrival. What Age Group is CMOM Designed For? CMOM is designed especially for children ages 0–6, a time of important brain development and growth. Our hands-on exhibits and programs support early learning through play, creativity, and exploration. While older children may enjoy select exhibits and programs, most of our spaces are specifically created for toddlers, preschoolers, and early elementary-age kids. We encourage grown-ups to play too! Food & Drink To keep our exhibits clean, safe for play, and free of allergens, food and beverages are not allowed inside the building. We do allow baby formula and water, and there are water bottle refill stations by the restrooms. While CMOM does not offer a cafeteria, you are welcome to leave and return throughout the day to enjoy nearby dining options and discount offers. Strollers For your convenience, complimentary stroller and coat check is available at CMOM. To ensure a safe and comfortable experience for all visitors, strollers are not permitted in exhibit areas. School Field Trips Visiting with a group of 15 or more students, campers, or a large group? On weekdays we offer specially curated 90-minute guided tours led by our expert educators. Advanced reservations are required to ensure the best experience for your group. Visit our Guided Field Trips page and contact our team for more information. Accessibility CMOM is committed to being a welcoming space for all visitors. The Museum is wheelchair accessible. Please note that the lower level of the Dynamic H2O exhibition has limited accessibility. Personal care attendants accompanying visitors with disabilities receive free admission. We offer a fully accessible restroom on the Third Floor and an ambulatory accessible restroom on the Lower Level. We also have accessible elevators and stroller parking. If you need assistance during your visit, our staff is happy to help. Personal care attendants accompanying visitors with disabilities receive free admission. Sensory Kits are also available to borrow at no additional cost during your visit. Each kit is designed to help children regulate, refocus, and feel at ease, and includes: Over-the-ear headphones for noise reduction A sand timer to support transitions Fidget toys to encourage self-regulation and focus Kits are available at the Admissions desk and in PlayWorks on the 3rd floor. Simply check one out at the start of your visit and return it before you leave. Learn more about our Accessibility Programing. Museum Policies To ensure a safe and enjoyable visit for everyone, we’ve put together a set of visitor guidelines. You can learn more on this page . Questions? Please visit our Frequently Asked Questions page. You can also call us at 212-721-1223 or send us an email to [email protected] . To help ensure everyone has a safe, fun, and welcoming experience , please review our visitor guidelines and helpful FAQs below . You’ll find important information on tickets, hours, museum policies, accessibility, and more — all organized in easy-to-browse sections to help you plan your visit. For general questions, please email us at [email protected] . Safe Space Policy & How to Reach Us Our shared commitment to kindness and respect CMOM is dedicated to providing a safe, welcoming, and respectful environment for all children and caregivers. Our mission is to foster curiosity, early development, and joy through inclusive, hands-on learning. We value the diversity of our community and expect all visitors to treat one another—and our staff—with respect and kindness, regardless of race, ethnicity, religion, national origin, gender identity, sexual orientation, or ability. To support a positive environment, we ask that visitors: Avoid verbal or physical confrontations Follow museum rules, including using designated stroller parking and no food/drink in exhibits Refrain from behavior that is threatening, disrespectful, discriminatory, or disruptive CMOM does not permit harassment, hate speech, racism, or any conduct that puts others at risk. Visitors who compromise the safety or well-being of others may be asked to leave, and in serious or repeated cases, access may be permanently revoked. Thank you for helping us ensure CMOM remains a safe and joyful space for all. Department Directory General Info: 212-721-1223 | [email protected] Ticketing | [email protected] Membership: 212-721-1234 | [email protected] Early Childhood Classes: 212-721-1226 | [email protected] Guided Group Visits: 212-721-1225 | [email protected] Development Department: 347-341-7458 | [email protected] Planning Your Visit When is the Museum open? October – June: Tuesday – Sunday, 10 am – 5 pm and federal holiday Mondays July – September: Monday – Sunday, 10 am – 5 pm Do I need a ticket to visit? Yes! Tickets to CMOM are easy to purchase and we participate with many programs to provide discounted and free admission . All visitors must have a ticket for entry. Visitors are allowed to re-enter the museum throughout the day of their visit. Members are required to show their membership card upon entry. Information on admission rates can be found in our Visit section. You can save one dollar by purchasing online in advance! Get Tickets! How do I visit with Cool Culture Pass? /If you have a Cool Culture Pass, please do the following for a seamless visit: The Cool Culture pass provides free general admission for up to 5 guests, including the card holder A valid photo ID is required to verify the Family Pass holder’s last name For groups of more than 5, admission fees apply to additional guests Nannies and caregivers may only use the Family Pass when the cardholder is present. Does CMOM have a cafe or dining facility on-site? No, CMOM does not have a café or dining area. However, you are welcome to leave and return throughout the day to enjoy nearby dining options where we have discounts available . Just ask for a return sticker from Security or Guest Services at the door! Can I bring food and drinks during my visit? No. For the safety and comfort of all visitors—especially those with food allergies— outside food and snacks are not permitted inside CMOM. We do allow water and baby formula . We kindly ask that you use spill-proof containers whenever possible to help protect our exhibits. We appreciate your cooperation in keeping our exhibits clean and safe for all children. Where can I store my stroller during my visit? We provide complimentary Stroller & Coat Check using Chexology, a digital system. This provides a more streamlined process for our visitors and attendants and everything is connected to your personal phone number! Is CMOM accessible for visitors with disabilities? Yes! CMOM is committed to providing an inclusive experience for all visitors. The museum is wheelchair accessible, however please note that the Lower Level of the Dynamic H2O exhibition has limited accessibility. We offer a fully accessible restroom on the Third Floor and an ambulatory accessible restroom on the Lower Level. We also have accessible elevators and stroller parking. If you need assistance during your visit, our staff is happy to help. Personal care attendants accompanying visitors with disabilities receive free admission. See more information about Accessibility on our website. Where are the restrooms located? Restrooms are available on the Lower Level and the Third Floor, both with infant changing tables. A fully wheelchair accessible restroom is available on the Third Floor, with an ambulatory accessible restroom on the Lower Level. How do I use my Access Pass and get a discounted ticket like Cool Culture? We are happy to work with a variety of programs like Cool Culture, etc. Just show your card at the desk and get your tickets. Currently you are not able to book these tickets on our website , but we always have tickets set-aside on-site for these partners! Check out our full list of partners. How do I redeem my ACM Reciprocal Ticket? All partner, discounted and complimentary tickets must be redeemed in person at our Admissions desk. For information on what programs we participate in and what offers each one provides, check out our page with more information. I left / lost something at the Museum! We have all been there! If we find items that are missing their owner, we keep lost items for 30 days at our Stroller & Coat Check area. To report or claim a lost item, please fill out our Lost & Found form . A team member will contact you if your item is found. Visitor Guidelines Can I help guide another child’s behavior if I see them doing something unsafe? We ask that adults only supervise their own children. If you have a concern about another visitor’s behavior, please notify a CMOM staff member—we’re here to help! First Aid kids are available on-site should they be needed. My child has special needs. Are there areas of the Museum suited for them? We know some children may need quieter areas. While CMOM can be lively, we encourage you to explore different spaces within the Museum or ask a staff member for suggestions on less busy areas. Sensory Kits are also available to borrow at no additional cost during your visit. Each kit is designed to help children regulate, refocus, and feel at ease. How can I make sure my child plays safely at CMOM? CMOM is designed for hands-on exploration, and we love seeing kids engaged and excited! To ensure a safe visit: Keep an eye on your child at all times. Encourage gentle play—exhibits and materials should be used with care. Climbing is only allowed in designated areas built for active play. Can my child run inside the Museum? We encourage movement and active play, but for safety, we ask that children walk while inside the Museum. There are plenty of fun spaces for climbing and jumping in designated areas! Why aren’t strollers allowed in exhibit areas? To ensure clear pathways and safe spaces for all visitors to move and play, we provide complimentary stroller check at the entrance. This helps keep our exhibits open and accessible for everyone. We also want to be sure that we have emergency exists always clear and not cause any fire and safety concerns. Health & Safety What happens if someone gets sick and we can't visit on the day of our tickets? We understand that illness happens, especially with our audience being little ones. Please reach out to [email protected] , and we will do our best to accommodate you to another date! For General Visitation tickets only. Registered programs and special events not included. Does my child need to wear shoes in all areas of the Museum? For health, safety, and cleanliness, we ask that children keep their shoes on throughout the museum, except in designated baby and toddler barefoot areas : Baby Grand Central (Lower Level) : Shoes must be removed before entering. Baby Steps in PlayWorks (Third Floor) : Babies and toddlers may be barefoot in this space. Does CMOM properly sanitize the spaces and provide hand sanitizer for guests? Yes! We take cleanliness very seriously and ensure that our spaces and the facility are cleaned regularly. We also provide hand sanitizer in a variety of easy-to-access locations for those who would like to use it. How often does CMOM clean the exhibits? We take cleanliness and hygiene seriously at CMOM! Our exhibits are cleaned daily throughout the day to ensure a safe and enjoyable experience for all visitors. Our Clean Team is on staff, regularly checking and sanitizing exhibit spaces, restrooms, and floors . You’ll often see them making their rounds to keep everything fresh and tidy, so you can focus on having fun! If you ever need assistance or notice something that needs attention, just let a staff member know—we’re happy to help What happens if my child gets hurt? In the case of anyone getting hurt, we have First Aid kits available on-site . Caregivers should ask any CMOM staff member for assistance and we are happy to provide help immediately. Membership & Discounts Do I need to reserve tickets in advance if I am a CMOM member? We encourage all members to reserve tickets online prior to arriving here at CMOM. Reserve your tickets here . Can I apply my admission ticket toward the cost of my CMOM Membership? Yes. This can be done within two weeks of your visit. Please visit our admission desk with your receipt or contact us at [email protected] or at 212-721-1234. Can I upgrade my Mini Membership? Yes. Up to one month after expiration, please contact us at [email protected] or at 212-721-1234. Can I purchase a membership as a gift? Yes. You can purchase a gift membership online here or contact us at [email protected] or 212-721-1234. What are the membership levels and benefits? Please visit the Membership page for more information. How do I find my digital membership card? You can access your digital membership card via the eMembership Card app using your Member ID for log in. Instructions to download your card can be found here. Can my caregiver bring the children to CMOM with my membership? Yes. Your caregiver can bring the children under your membership. Please provide the caregiver with a print or digital copy of the reservation confirmation email and the digital membership card. How can I update the information on my membership? Please contact us at [email protected] or 212-721-1234. What if I cannot find my membership ID? Please contact us at [email protected] or 212-721-1234, and we can retrieve your membership number. Can we transfer or get a refund on our membership? No. All memberships to the CMOM are nontransferable and nonrefundable. We are appreciative of your support as members, and your membership helps fund our mission and keeps CMOM accessible to all families. I am using my local library’s CMOM membership. What do I need to do? We encourage you to reserve a ticket on our website using the member ID provided by your library. Upon arrival, please present a copy of your reservation confirmation email and the pass provided to you by your library. I am a member of another Museum in the Association for Children’s Museums. Can I get discounted admission? Yes. Please email [email protected] for more information. My company is a corporate member. How can I reserve tickets? We encourage you to reserve a ticket on our website using the member ID provided by your company. Upon arrival, please present a copy of your reservation confirmation email. If you do not have a reservation, you must present a photo ID company badge upon arrival. Your caregiver can bring the children to the Museum under your company’s corporate membership. Please provide the caregiver with a print or digital copy of the reservation confirmation email. Does CMOM accept corporate matching gifts? Yes. You can double the amount of your membership contribution through your employer’s matching gifts program. For more information, please contact us at [email protected] or call us at 212-721-1234. Education & Classes Does CMOM provide classes? Yes! We have year round registered classes for children with our wonderful educators. You can sign-up for email to stay notified when registration opens, and visit our Education page to learn more. Are there drop-off camps? Currently, we do not provide drop-off camps. I would love to bring my school to CMOM! We have programs throughout the year for School Groups and Camps during the Summer. Sign-up for email and bookmark this page to learn more about the offerings. Would CMOM come to my school for a program? CMOM hosts a variety of School Residencies where we come to your schools and bring selected curriculum into your facility, for your students! Learn more about options here. Other Common Questions Can I host my child's birthday party at CMOM? At this time, we no longer offer birthday party services. However, we invite you to explore our variety of other programs and events designed for families and children. What else can we do around CMOM? The Upper West Side is filled with wonderful restaurants, parks, and other cultural institutions to visit. Plan your day at CMOM and include a visit to one of two great parks nearby. Riverside Park’s entrance on 83rd Street has a beautiful playground and ample benches for picnics. Three blocks east of the Museum is Central Park where there are ball fields, fountains, playgrounds and plenty of space for picnicking. CMOM has a list of restaurants with discounts and offers. Check them out for your next visit! Does CMOM donate memberships or free passes to my organization? CMOM recognizes that there are many wonderful organizations supporting children in the tri-state area. We are happy to donate a limited number of complimentary memberships. Please email [email protected] for more information. Is CMOM moving? Yes! CMOM will be moving in 2028 to a fabulous larger building on 96th and Central Park West. Until then we look forward to seeing you and your family at 83rd street! Learn more about our future home.
